# Inherited fixed marker constructor

An abstract nongeneric owner extends a plain parent and implements an empty
interface. Its private constructor accepts a concrete Value, a long, a boolean,
and Sink<Value>. Its public marker constructor forwards every original input
word to that fixed private target. A witnessed synthetic-flag-only edit preserves
all original Code and metadata. A child calls the marker constructor and supplies
a virtual callback while child fields still contain their allocation defaults.

Frozen direct, compiled-caller, reflection and method-handle observers check
superclass publication and failures, fixed callback identity, wide and boolean
arguments, null inputs, nullable/non-null markers, partial fields, and exact
exception identity. Independent wrong programs change one argument, narrow the
long, move the child stamp early, or omit superclass effects. The declaration
variant imports the original Base, Tagged, Sink and Value classes. All sources
are independently authored and contain no application data.

The `--open-owner` variant copies the authored sources into a fresh directory,
makes Core concrete and keeps its public class open to subclassing. The original
Child observations still require its virtual callback during Core construction.
A separate frozen observer also constructs Core directly through all four call
routes, checking its own callback, full long extrema, boolean and marker values,
and partial field identity. Both declaration modes run 60 cases twice per stage;
all metadata remains exact except the explicitly reported synthetic flag.
The `--final-owner` variant uses a package-private final Core and removes the
copied child. Same-package ordinary, frozen, reflective and method-handle callers
check all 56 cases twice per stage with owned and imported parent declarations.
The observer retains superclass publication, callback order, full long words,
boolean and marker inputs, partial fields and exact exception identity. Five
independent wrong programs alter a reference or boolean, truncate the long,
reorder the callback or remove a superclass effect. All original metadata remains
exact except the reported marker synthetic flag.

The `--variant-input` profiles keep a nested wildcard contract in the original
private constructor: Sink<? super Value, ? extends Box<? super Object,
? extends Object>>. The copied Sink and new Box declarations each retain two
Object-bounded parameters. The first callback slot preserves the original
runtime observer, while frozen reflection verifies every nested argument.
Abstract and open owners run with owned and immutable dependency declarations;
the synthetic flag remains the only reported metadata difference.
